# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# A REFERENCE ERROR SHAPE, NOT A SERVED FIXTURE -- see error-not-open.json. The --fail argument that
# produces it:
#     fmonero-mock --role wallet --fail transfer=-17:'not enough money'
# and DESIGN.md §8's Phase 1b gate uses the same code on get_balance to prove the error map end to
# end: --fail get_balance=-17:'not enough money' must make `fmonero wallet balance` exit 14.
# CODE: -17 = WALLET_RPC_ERROR_CODE_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_error_codes.h:50).
# MESSAGE: handle_rpc_exception catches tools::error::not_enough_money and sets er.message = e.what()
#         (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:3797-3801). what() is the string the transfer_error base
#         was constructed with -- "not enough money" (src/wallet/wallet_errors.h:518), lower case, no
#         period. The class ALSO has a to_string() that appends ", available = ..., tx_amount = ..."
#         (:527-534), but that is NOT what reaches the wire through what().
#         So a client must not expect the amounts to be in the message, and fmonero does not parse
#         them out: it maps the CODE and prints the message verbatim.
# -17 MAPS TO EXIT 14 insufficient_funds, with the hint `fmonero wallet balance` (§1b.4, §4a). So does
#         -37 NOT_ENOUGH_UNLOCKED_MONEY, whose message comes from the sibling catch at
#         :3802-3805 -- the two are DIFFERENT conditions with the SAME exit: "you do not have it" and
#         "you have it but it is not spendable yet". The distinguishing information is in the message
#         and in get_balance's unlocked_balance (get_balance-locked.json), not in the exit code.
# EXIT 14 IS NOT A BUG REPORT: it is the ordinary answer to sending more than you hold, and the hint
#         is the command that shows what you do hold.
